positions.as_written: Ask what imaging they have had: radiographs, ultrasound, magnetic resonance, computed tomography, or a scan they cannot name.
Ask when, and whether it was before or after any treatment.
Ask whether the images are available or only the report, because a report is a interpretation and the images can be reviewed.
Ask what they were told, in their words, and listen for the phrase that has stuck.
Take the history before reading the report wherever possible, which is awkward and is the only way to get an uncontaminated account.
At decision level the imaging history determines whether anything further is needed, which is a question that should be asked more often.
